race_context: The state list's 'Sullivan Southwest School Board' is the Southwest School Corporation (SWSC) in Sullivan County, which runs Carlisle Elementary and Carlisle Middle schools and Sullivan Elementary (with a preschool), Sullivan Middle and Sullivan High schools {in_list}{st_sep2026}. State enrollment counts were 1,800 students in 2023-24, 1,776 in 2024-25 and 1,785 in 2025-26 {idoe_enroll}. In August 2026 the district reported 217 students at the Carlisle schools and 1,542 at the Sullivan schools {st_aug2026}.
Superintendent: Chris Stitzle, with Assistant Superintendent Jon Stuckey {st_aug2026}{wtwo_stitzle}.

The board has five members. Those voting at the Sept. 16, 2026 meeting were Jon Bobbitt (president), Mike Eslinger, Jerry Wilson, Detrich Harris and Jaque Steele {st_aug2026}{st_sep2026}. Seats are staggered: two members were elected in 2018 and 2022 (Jerry D. Wilson and Michael J. Eslinger both times), and three in 2020 and 2024 (Jon H. Bobbitt, Leigh Detrich Harris and Jacqueline L. Steele in 2024) {enr_2018}{enr_2022}{enr_2020}{enr_2024}. This guide could not load the district's board page and did not find which townships each numbered district covers or whether all district voters vote in every race.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: District 1 and District 5, one seat each, matching the state list's 'vote for 1' and the two seats filled in 2022 {in_list}{enr_2022}. Wilson is running in District 5 against Derrick Demoss, who also ran against him in 2022 (Wilson 1,851 votes, DeMoss 1,461) {in_list}{enr_2022}. Eslinger, the other member elected in 2022, is not on the 2026 list, so District 1 appears to be an open seat contested by Colt Thompson and Melissa Stearley; this guide did not confirm which district Eslinger represents {in_list}{ic_list}.
Party labels: all four candidates filed without a party and are listed as Nonpartisan; 2026 is the first year Indiana school board candidates could list one {ic_list}{in_list}{st_party}.

Facilities (August 2026): at an Aug. 19, 2026 public hearing the board approved a lease/bond-financed project that includes four new primary classrooms, four new intermediate classrooms and a commons area and an expanded office at Sullivan Elementary, renovated PE and athletic locker rooms at Sullivan High School and other district-wide work. The district's municipal advisor said issuing the new bonds is not projected to raise the tax rate. No one from the public commented {st_aug2026}.

Budget (August–September 2026): the treasurer's report in August showed about $5.1 million in total cash, including $2.08 million in the Education Fund, $1.17 million in the Operations Fund and $1.48 million in the Rainy Day Fund {st_aug2026}. The board approved a 4% overall health insurance increase for 2026-27 and adopted the 2027 budget on Sept. 16, 2026 after a Sept. 2 hearing {st_aug2026}{st_sep2026}. This guide found no reporting on how the 2025 property-tax law SEA 1 affects SWSC, and no SWSC referendum.

Staffing and parent concerns (2026): the board held its required hearing on teacher collective bargaining on Aug. 19, 2026 {st_aug2026}. At the Sept. 16 meeting a parent raised transportation problems for a second time; Eslinger said administrators planned to review and adjust bus routes after fall break. Another parent spoke about tutoring and reading help {st_sep2026}.

Forums: this guide found no 2026 candidate forum, questionnaire or voter-guide entries for these races. The Sullivan Daily Times' 2026 coverage found by this guide did not cover the school board races.
